thread:
maria.g: heads up — our SCIM backfill in staging started failing after the RBAC attribute change. ~500 users errored, most 409 (duplicate) and some 500 (KMS decrypt).
alex: :eyes: which IdP and which attribute was changed? any repro user IDs?
maria.g: Azure AD -> SCIM /Users. We normalized the externalId to lowercase in the RBAC change (PR 4321). Affected users have mixed-case extIds in AD.

maria.g: sample error we see from the provisioner:
```
2026-03-20T14:01:12Z WARN provisioning-service scim=PUT /Users/33421 status=409 body="externalId conflict: extId already exists for user 9988"
2026-03-20T14:01:12Z ERROR kms decrypt failed err="context mismatch" key_alias=projects/redwood/keys/scim-provisioner
```
alex: ok that 409 makes sense if extId normalization changed — two AD accounts mapping to same normalized externalId. KMS decrypt looks unrelated but could block retries. jordan: can you confirm whether the extId collision is in our DB or coming from the IdP response?

maria.g: collisions are being thrown by our DB unique constraint (users.external_id_idx). IdP is sending two distinct AD objects: one with ExtID 'John.Doe' and another 'john.doe'. After normalization both become 'john.doe' -> conflict.

jordan: twofold: 1) for immediate relief we can disable the normalization flag in the staging provisioner to allow case-sensitive extId until we run a backfill/merge. 2) investigate KMS decrypt: samir, think the KMS errors are due to a missing decryption context after the RBAC rollout?

samir: saw the same in logs. KMS errors are intermittent: "context mismatch" from CloudKMS when decrypting the SCIM envelope. I suspect the provisioner started using a new encryption context key 'rbac-v2' after the feature flip but older records were encrypted with 'rbac-v1'.

samir: quick check command I ran: `gcloud kms decrypt --ciphertext-file=blob.bin --location=global --keyring=infra --key=scim-provisioner --additional-auth-data=rbac-v1` returned cleartext. Using `rbac-v2` fails.

maria.g: that matches timing: PR 4321 rotated the provisioner AAD token and toggled a flag that switched the encryption context. Ops: any changes to KMS aliases in the last 48h?

ops-oncall: no KMS alias rotations in prod, but staging pipeline ran a config change that added `rbac_version=2` to the env for the staging provisioner. I reverted the env on the staging workers already (rolled back to r-20260319-5).

idp-bot: automated-alert: SCIM provisioner group sync rate high — 512 errors in 1h (created_at >= 2026-03-20T13:00Z). Ticket created: #INC-20260320-78

alex: good. For the long-term: we need a migration strategy to canonicalize extId without dropping or duplicating entitlement state. Options: 1) map AD objects to canonical extId and merge duplicates; 2) maintain case-sensitive extId in DB but normalize for routing; 3) update IdP provisioning to normalize upstream. Thoughts?

jordan: prefer canonicalization + merge. We should run a dry-run merge script in staging: identify collisions (case variants), pick authoritative object (most recent login / AD primary), merge memberships, then reingest.

samir: agree. Also need to re-encrypt older records with the new KMS context (rbac-v2) or maintain backward-compatibility by trying both contexts during decrypt. Simple fix: provisioner tries decrypt with v2 then falls back to v1.

maria.g: I'll open a small PR that adds fallback decrypt; ops please keep rbac_version env at v1 until backfill completes. I'll prepare the merge script and a dry-run report.

ops-oncall: rbac_version pinned to v1 in staging. I also increased provisioning worker concurrency to speed up retry backfill.

alex: for audit/compliance: we must record the merge and any autoritative decisions in the audit log (who, why, before/after extId). Maria please include a CSV snapshot and attach to ticket INC-20260320-78.

maria.g: will do. Also opening vuln-triage note: the KMS fallback behavior should be explicitly tested — failure to decrypt could lead to partial provisioning and possible stale RBAC state. I'll add a test case.

jordan: one more: check SCIM patch vs put behavior — some of the failing requests were PUTs that replace user object, causing membership flicker during retries. For sensitive groups, use PATCH with merge semantics.

samir: noted. I'll add logic to prefer PATCH when updating group membership on collisions.

maria.g: summary of immediate actions: 1) ops pinned rbac_version=v1 in staging (done), 2) samir adds decrypt fallback (PR incoming), 3) maria will run collision-detection dry-run and produce merge CSV, 4) alex/jordan to review merge plan and audit entries, 5) increase monitoring and attach to INC ticket.

ops-oncall: rolling redeploy to pick up decrypt-fallback PR once approved. ETA 30m.

alex: if everything in staging looks good, we schedule prod cutover with a maintenance window and support from SRE and security on call.

maria.g: thanks all. I'll post the dry-run report here when ready. Closing interim updates until then. :white_check_mark:
